method: Two connected Sera task-to-account sequences, twelve complete spoken stages; actual delivered clips and ward/quiet music and ward ambience. Settled normal-focus approximation: Voice70/Music60/Ambience50, source gains from runtime, music/room source .5/.35, speech duck .22/.44, 120ms same-speaker gaps and one-second stage separators.
limitations: Offline preview omits browser fades, download timing and hardware. Original account recordings and new-23.5LUFS clips are not level matched. No independent listening/acting score or comprehension finding is inferred.

scenes.text:
Sera has a hand on the back of her chair. From the doorway, the wall is only a strip of wet light. A tray of blank question cards waits on the visitor side; the source folders are closed behind her.

"I keep sending people to the wall. I would like to stand there myself for once. But I cannot leave this table open."

You can carry the cards to the wall while she keeps custody here, or watch the closed table while she listens. Either task takes you away from drafting for a moment. Neither earns money or standing.

scenes.text:
Sera slides the tray across the visitor side. The cards are blank; none is a source or an approved witness account.

"Take the blank cards. Bring back the empty tray too. People should have somewhere to put a question when they find one."

The wall is a short walk from the table. You can make that trip, choose the other task, or leave this work with Sera.

scenes.text:
The cards stay at the wall. Back at the table, you set down the empty tray. Sera moves her pencil out of its way.

"You brought the tray back empty. That is all right. An empty place for a question is still worth keeping."

She draws the blank cover sheet toward you. Now there is room for the account, if you still want to prepare it.

Sera puts a blank public cover sheet beside the recorder and your sources. 'The names can be spoken either way. This is a different promise: an account someone can question after you leave.'

First decide what the sources support. Then decide whose words can appear on the sheet.

Sera leaves the recorder running. The mechanic waits for the source you can point to; a witness's address stays off the table.

scenes.text:
Sera closes the tray drawer. The folders remain on her side of the table. She waits until you have taken a place facing the doorway.

"Stay on this side. If someone asks for a source, ask them to wait for me. You do not have to answer for anybody."

You are keeping a place, not taking custody of the sources. Wait for her return, choose the other task, or leave the table with her.

Sera comes back through the doorway and takes her place on the source side. You have left the closed folders where they were.

"I heard the voices from the wall instead of through this doorway. Thank you for staying."

She draws the blank cover sheet toward you. The account is still yours to prepare or leave.
